Develop with ...Be7 (mistake).phrase: but this move was a mistake
Develop with ...Be7 (mistake).note: Never says why it was a mistake. The line it was shown has White taking two pawns (6.Nxe5 and 8.Nxc6), but the coach doesn't point that out.

Develop with ...Be7 (mistake).phrase: challenge your knight on c6 with Bxc6
Develop with ...Be7 (mistake).note: Bxc6 captures your knight (that's in the facts). “Challenge” hides that you lose it and have to take back.

Scholar's mate trap: ...Nf6?? (blunder).phrase: placed your king in a difficult position
Scholar's mate trap: ...Nf6?? (blunder).note: Vague. The real point: White's queen (h5) and bishop (c4) both hit f7, and ...Nf6 does nothing about it. Our board facts don't report that, so the coach couldn't say it.
A beginner is shown “−100.00”. It should just say White has a forced checkmate. Our code tells the coach “a forced mate for White”, but it still printed the number.

...Nxe4? loses material (mistake).phrase: you should aim to capture the pawn on f2 and attack their queen
...Nxe4? loses material (mistake).note: Makes ...Nxf2 sound good, but the coach stops just before White wins that knight: the line goes on 8.Rxe5+ Be6 9.Kxf2 (press ▶ to the end). Our level cut hid the punchline.

...Nxe4? loses material (mistake).phrase: Bxc6+, putting your king in check
...Nxe4? loses material (mistake).note: Leaves out that Bxc6+ also captures your knight on c6 (it's in the facts).

Premature 3.Ng5?? (blunder).phrase: You should then play d4, which opens a line for your bishop on c1.
Premature 3.Ng5?? (blunder).note: The move comes before its idea (your rule: idea first). And the real point of 4.d4 is that your bishop on c1 now attacks the queen on g5. That only becomes clear in the next sentence.

Premature 3.Ng5?? (blunder).phrase: inviting a pawn attack on a6
Premature 3.Ng5?? (blunder).note: Garbled: the fact is that Black could attack the bishop by pushing a7–a6. It's also odd to name only a downside of the move you should have played.

Italian Game (Giuoco Piano).note: True but minor. The main idea of 4.c3 is to support d4, which the line plays two moves later.
